To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the XMM-Newton data reveal the following: (i) The X-ray emission of the Pleiades stars is dominated by a few bright sources, which are mostly solar-like stars, and the X-ray spectra of the brightest stars can be modelled with coronae with temperatures of a few million degrees and a low metallicity.

(i) the X-ray luminosity-rotation relation is valid down to a level of L X ~ 2 × 10 29erg s -1; (ii) the X-ray emission of intermediate-type Pleiads can be explained by the presence of active solar-like companions; (iii) the coronal temperature of solar-type stars increases from the slowly rotating to the rapidly rotating regime, and (iv) the coronae of solar-like stars are metal-poor.

(1) the Pleiades are a valuable laboratory for the study of stellar activity in the solar mass range; (2) the Pleiadean solar-like stars are a valuable laboratory in which to study the effects of rotation on stellar coronal structure; (3) the Pleiads provide a sample of intermediate-type stars that are useful in the study of coronal evolution in the mass range 0.5–1.5 M �.
